title: Customer ask ensemble & test lab — July 2028
content:
TL;DR:
A compact synthesis of recent customer signals (support logs, pilot interviews, usage telemetry, exit surveys) focused on inference reliability, cost controls, and rollout observability. This doc proposes a small experiments backlog (the "test lab") to validate 3 cross-cutting feature proposals: a low-latency routing toggle, per-route cost-visibility, and a model-variant fallback manifest for private deployments.

Context & signal sources (ensemble approach):
- Support transcripts (May–Jun 2028): ~40 escalations mentioning "unexpected latency spikes" and lack of visibility when fallback runs.
- Pilot interviews (4 customers: fintech, healthcare, search-saas, internal partner): qualitative demand for deterministic latency guarantees and easier rollback.
- Telemetry snapshot (redwood:prod, 2028-06): 95p latency variance increased 18% during peak batch windows; 60% of spikes correlate with cross-customer batching bursts.
- Exit survey excerpts: two churned pilots citing "cost unpredictability during bursts" and "unclear model downgrade behavior".

Synthesis: emergent themes
1) Predictable latency over raw throughput is becoming a hard requirement for low-latency customer apps.
2) Customers need per-route, token-level cost attribution surfaced in the Console and API analytics.
3) Rollout failures (canary -> full) are risky because fallbacks are opaque; customers want explicit fallback manifests and dry-run testing.
4) Many asks are interdependent: routing policy, batching heuristics, and KV-cache invalidation behavior combine to produce surprise latency/cost.

Prioritized feature proposals (impact / rough effort):
- A: Low-latency routing toggle (impact: high, effort: medium)
  - Brief: Add a per-route config that prefers low-latency nodes and disables batching thresholds for strict SLOs.
  - Key success metric: reduce 95p latency by >=30% on routes that opt-in, without increasing token cost >10%.
  - Risks: throughput drop for shared pools; need throttling policies.

- B: Per-route tokenized-cost breakdown (impact: high, effort: low–medium)
  - Brief: Expose token cost by model variant and route in the Console and via a new billing endpoint.
  - Success metric: customer-reported clarity score improves in follow-up interviews; internal tickets about "mystery charges" drop 50%.
  - Dependencies: billing events tagging, SDK additions.

- C: Fallback manifest + dry-run validation (impact: medium, effort: medium–high)
  - Brief: A declarative manifest that defines fallback chains (model variant, region, capacity tier) and a dry-run mode to validate compatibility before rollouts.
  - Success metric: rollback time reduced by 40%, fewer post-rollout incident pages.
  - Risks: compatibility matrix complexity across private deployments.

Micro-experiments (Test Lab) — 6 week plan (fast cycles):
Week 1–2 (MVP experiments)
- Launch B (cost breakdown) as a Console beta for 3 customers (fintech pilot + 2 early adopters). Instrument satisfaction survey. Owner: Priya.
- Quick hack: client-side flag to route to low-latency pool (server-side toggle later) for 1 internal partner to validate latency delta. Owner: Marco.
Week 3–4
- Prototype A server-side toggle on a shadow route to observe throughput and 95p impact. Add throttling guard rails. Owner: Tomás (infra) + Marco.
- Start design for C: define YAML manifest schema and integration tests. Owner: Dana.
Week 5–6
- Run dry-run tests for C against a private deployment (staging) with small corpus. Validate error modes.
- Consolidate learnings and prepare a customer-facing one-pager and a recommended rollout pattern. Owner: Elena.

Acceptance criteria & success metrics (per experiment):
- A: 95p latency improvement >=30% on opt-in routes, token cost delta measured, no more than 2 significant incidents in 30 days.
- B: Console shows per-route cost; 3 pilot customers can reconcile charges end-to-end; CS ticket volume for unexplained costs down 50%.
- C: Dry-run correctly flags incompatible fallbacks in >=90% of seeded incompatibility cases; can apply manifest rollback in <=10 minutes.

Sample customer quotes (anonymized) observed across channels:
- "We need to set a latency floor — sometimes the model switches and our user flows get choppy."
- "I'd pay for visibility at the route level — token costs are what keep me up at night."
- "Rollouts felt like black magic; we couldn't see what fallback happened when traffic spiked."

Open questions & trade-offs:
- How aggressive should throttling be when low-latency toggles reduce batch sizes? (SLO vs unit cost trade-off)
- For private deployments, do we offer a vetted fallback catalog or let customers declare any variant?
- Do we charge for per-route billing visibility as an add-on or include it in the Console?

Dependencies & blockers:
- Billing events tagging (billing infra team) — JIRA-BILL-1998
- Dedicated pool capacity for low-latency experiments (infra scheduling)
- Model variant compatibility matrix (applied-ml input) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-compat/pull/58

Next steps (short list):
1) Align with Product & Infra: quick sync (30m) to get buy-in and capacity (owners: Elena + Tomás) — target by 2028-07-18.
2) Recruit 3 pilot customers for the Console beta (Priya).
3) Create a small telemetry dashboard (Marco) to show 50th/95th/99th latency and cost deltas per route.
4) Draft the fallback manifest YAML spec and post to Confluence for review (Dana).

Notes to self / rough TODOs: 
- Draft customer-facing one-pager after Week 2.
- Collate top 10 support transcripts into appendix for Product review.
- Get legal sign-off if cost telemetry surfaces per-user PII (privacy check).

Appendix: quick impact-effort table (scratch)
- Low-latency routing toggle: Impact High / Effort Medium => Priority: 1
- Per-route cost breakdown: Impact High / Effort Low => Priority: 0 (fast win)
- Fallback manifest: Impact Medium / Effort Medium-High => Priority: 2

Slack threads / refs: #cs-pilots, #infra-latency, #billing-api
Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/ask-ensemble-2028
Jira seeds: JIRA-CS-4821, JIRA-ROUTE-334, JIRA-BILL-1998

Owner matrix (proposal):
- Elena Park (owner, synthesis + comms)
- Priya Nair (pilot recruitment + customer QA)
- Marco Ruiz (telemetry + quick routing prototype)
- Tomás Ortega (infra gating + pool configuration)
- Dana Liu (manifest spec + product design)

If you read nothing else: focus on shipping per-route cost visibility (B) as a fast instrument to reduce churn risk and buy time while we validate routing/fallback patterns.

-- Elena

(End of doc)
